sources.entry: FixStat - Menu bar monitor and diagnostics for Mac repair: per-model sensor names, battery cell data, SSD SMART including USB drives, panic history and guided hardware tests. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/BurakFixLab/fixstat) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.one_liner: FixStat is a free, open-source macOS menu bar monitor for board-level Mac repair, showing battery, temperature, fan and SSD data with per-model sensor names and diagnostic tests.
summary.what_it_does: FixStat displays battery, temperature, fan and system data in the macOS menu bar, using sensor names mapped per Mac model where verified and marked as estimated otherwise. A technician mode exposes raw battery gauge values (design and raw max capacity, cycle count, cell voltages, current) and every sensor with its raw SMC or HID key, grouped by component. Diagnostics include SSD health (NVMe and AHCI/SATA SMART, including SATA drives in USB enclosures), a memory test, kernel panic and shutdown history, a battery capacity discharge test, sleep/wake battery drain analysis, and a live monitor that charts up to six SMC values with CSV recording. A guided hardware check covers keyboard, trackpad, display, speakers, microphone, camera, fans under load, temperature sensors, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and USB ports. Results can be exported as PDF, CSV or JSON, with serial numbers masked by default. The README states the app is read-only with respect to the SMC and needs no administrator rights, except for an optional full SSD surface scan.
use_cases: diagnose a Mac with overheating or fan problems
check battery health and cycle count on a MacBook
verify SSD health of an internal or USB drive
run a post-repair stress test on a Mac
find out why a Mac kept panicking or shutting down
inspect a used Mac before buying it
how_to_run: Download FixStat.dmg from the Releases page at github.com/Lapsely/fixstat and drag FixStat to Applications
Open the app once, then approve it under System Settings > Privacy & Security (Open Anyway), or run: xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/FixStat.app
To build from source (macOS 14+, Xcode 16+): git clone the repo, cd fixstat, run scripts/build-app.sh
Command line: swift build -c release, then .build/release/sensordump
notable: Per-model verified sensor map: sensor names checked by load tests on a specific Mac model, with verified and estimated labels shown in the UI
Technician mode with raw battery gauge data, cell voltage imbalance warning, and raw SMC/HID keys for each sensor
Read-only design: no SMC write, no fan control, no root; the README describes the write command as not implemented
Runs on Intel Macs from macOS 10.13 and Apple Silicon from macOS 11, as one universal app
Battery history from the last hour up to 30 days plus a daily health log kept indefinitely
caveats: Not notarized by Apple, so the first launch needs a manual approval step or a quarantine-removal command
Apple Silicon temperatures rely on IOHIDEventSystemClient, a private API, so the app is not on the App Store
Intel sensor names are still estimated per the README, and many Macs show only estimated (not verified) sensor names
Full SSD surface scan requires the user's password and Full Disk Access
